inputs.declared_question: Can the existing Polis and Community Notes proposals be followed to exact passages in Field Notes 14 and 25?

internal_region.title: Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

sources_checked.title: Polis: Scaling Deliberation by Mapping High Dimensional Opinion Spaces
Community Notes public repository and guide source

source_facts.claim: The Polis repository describes an open-source platform for large-scale, open-ended feedback and links its methods paper on mapping high-dimensional opinion spaces.
The Community Notes repository publicly hosts program documentation and the open-source scoring implementation, and describes differing points of view as essential to helpful context.
Field Note 14 names Community Notes as an open reference for cross-perspective helpfulness, while Field Note 25 imagines inquiry that may preserve explicit disagreement rather than end in consensus.
source_facts.locator: The Open Anatomy; Expeditions, Storms, and the Birth of Boroughs

cartographer.inference: The three existing proposed edges remain useful, bounded comparisons. Polis and Community Notes offer distinct methods for finding structure across disagreement, while the field notes imagine a broader system of provenance, values, testimony, and preserved dissent.
cartographer.uncertainty: The proposals remain model-proposed and do not establish equivalence, endorsement, partnership, or a settled architectural choice.
cartographer.attribution: External facts come from the projects' public repositories and linked primary research. Internal facts come from the exact public Cyberdelic OS source.
cartographer.no_proposal_reason: The bounded source recheck supported the existing candidates and revealed no additional node or edge that would deepen this region.
